R-accessibility-1 (Field errors are conveyed by a red border only, with no text) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it

findings.evidence:
An invalid field gets the class
`field--invalid`, a red border (`#e5484d`); the list of errors at the top of
the page is removed, since the red border already shows where the problem
is. No message text is added, to keep the form compact.
findings.recommendation: Errors by colour only (WCAG 1.4.1 Use of Color, 3.3.1 Error Identification, 1.3.1 Info and Relationships, 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value). A screen reader user who tabs out of the postcode field with `ABC` hears nothing, and on returning to it hears only "Postcode, edit text": nothing says it is invalid or why. A colour-blind user cannot tell the red `#e5484d` border from the grey one, and no user learns what a valid postcode is, since the rule messages that `rules.ts` returns (today shown in the summary) are no longer displayed anywhere. Add a short text message under each invalid field (the rule's message), tie it to the input with `aria-describedby`, set `aria-invalid="true"` on the input, and keep the red border only as a supplement. Update the spec scenarios "An invalid postcode" and "A corrected field" — which today assert only "the field's border turns red" / "returns to grey" — and task 1.2 to require and test the message and `aria-invalid`.
findings.title: Field errors are conveyed by a red border only, with no text

findings.recommendation: Today the summary is the only announced feedback (`web/src/checkout/Form.tsx:22` renders `<div role="alert" className="error-summary">`). The plan removes it and says nothing of what happens on submit. A keyboard or screen reader user who presses Enter on "Pay" with a field they never left (validation runs on `blur` only) gets no announcement and focus stays on the button: the payment silently does not happen (WCAG 3.3.1 Error Identification, 4.1.3 Status Messages, 2.4.3 Focus Order). State in the design that submit still validates every field and either moves focus to the first invalid field (whose message is then read through `aria-describedby`, see R-accessibility-1) or keeps a summary with `role="alert"` linking to the fields; add a spec scenario and a task for it.
findings.title: Removing the error summary leaves a failed submit unannounced and without focus
